findings.title: Feed HTML is stored and rendered completely unsanitized (stored XSS)
findings.body: Feed item content is imported with no sanitization: poll_feed unescapes entities via CGI.unescapeHTML, then TopicEmbed.import stores the string as the post raw with cook_method raw_html, and Post#cook returns raw unchanged for raw_html posts. The result is rendered unsanitized both on the forum (the app renders post.cooked unescaped, trusting the normal cooking pipeline to have sanitized it) and in app/views/embed/best.html.erb via <%= raw post.cooked %>, which is served from the Discourse origin inside the iframe. Any <script> or event handler attribute in a feed entry — from a hostile or compromised blog/feed, a rogue author on a multi-author blog, or a MITM on a plaintext feed URL — becomes stored XSS executing in the forum origin as viewing users/admins. CGI.unescapeHTML makes it worse by converting the feed's safely entity-escaped markup into live tags. Imported content must be sanitized (e.g., with the already-bundled sanitize gem) before being stored as raw HTML.

findings.title: Unescaped URL interpolated into a single-quoted href in the imported footer
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import appends a footer to every imported post: #{url}. The only validation on url is a /^https?:\/\// prefix check, so a URL containing a single quote (e.g. from a malicious feed or a fetched page URL) breaks out of the attribute and injects arbitrary HTML into the post body, which is then rendered raw via the raw_html cook path. Because the footer is appended after Readability extraction, this vector bypasses even the limited tag/attribute filtering that import_remote applies to article content. The URL should be HTML/attribute-escaped before interpolation.

findings.title: Unauthenticated endpoint triggers remote fetch and topic creation; referer check is trivially spoofable
findings.body: GET /embed/best enqueues a RetrieveTopic job for any embed_url with no existing embed, with no authentication and no rate limiting. The only gate is that the Referer host matches embeddable_host, which any non-browser client can spoof (curl -H 'Referer: http://blog.example.com' ...). The 60-second Redis throttle in TopicRetriever is per-URL, so an attacker can supply unlimited distinct URLs on the embeddable host: each one makes the server fetch that page and create a forum topic as the embed_by_username user (topic spam, bandwidth/CPU amplification), and when feed_polling_enabled is on each request also triggers a synchronous full PollFeed run inside the job. Consider per-IP rate limiting and/or restricting which paths are importable.

findings.title: i.content is nil for RSS items without content:encoded, crashing the hourly job
findings.body: i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content:encoded/content element — plain RSS 2.0 feeds that only provide <description> are common, and SimpleRSS returns nil for absent elements. Because the job sets sidekiq_options retry: false, the exception kills the run silently until the next hour and any remaining items are never imported. Fall back to i.description (and/or i.summary) when content is absent. The new poll_feed_spec only exercises the site-setting gates and never parses a feed item, so this path is untested.

findings.title: embed.js/embed.css are never added to config.assets.precompile — feature 404s/500s in production
findings.body: The PR adds app/assets/javascripts/embed.js and app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss and references them via stylesheet_link_tag 'embed' (in the embed layout) and as the script embedding sites load, but no config change adds 'embed.js' or 'embed.css' to the asset precompile list. With the application's explicit precompile list and assets.compile disabled in production, /embed/best will raise AssetNotPrecompiledError and the embed snippet URL will 404, so the entire feature is broken in production. Add both assets to config.assets.precompile.

findings.title: add_column with default on posts rewrites the whole table under an exclusive lock
findings.body: add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false causes PostgreSQL (pre-11) to rewrite every row of the posts table to materialize the default, holding an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the duration. posts is typically the largest table in a Discourse database, so on busy installs this migration can block all writes to posts for minutes during deploy. Add the column without a default/NOT NULL, backfill in batches, then apply the default and constraint.

findings.title: open(url) used without requiring open-uri on the retrieve path
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url), but this file never requires 'open-uri' — only poll_feed.rb does. The HTTP-retrieve path (EmbedController → RetrieveTopic job → TopicRetriever#fetch_http → TopicEmbed.import_remote) therefore only works if Jobs::PollFeed happened to be loaded already; in lazy-loading environments (dev/test, or any process that never referenced PollFeed) Kernel#open treats the URL as a filename and raises Errno::ENOENT. Add require 'open-uri' to topic_embed.rb (or lib/topic_retriever.rb) so the dependency is explicit.

findings.title: embeddable_host is compared as an exact string against URI#host with no normalization
findings.body: The check URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host compares the parsed host against free-form admin text. Values admins commonly paste — 'http://example.com', 'example.com/', or 'example.com:8080' — never equal URI#host ('example.com'), so every legitimate embed is rejected with 'invalid referer host' and no diagnostics. The same strict comparison in TopicRetriever.invalid_host? also fails when the blog's canonical URL host differs from the page host (www vs apex), producing the infinite loading screen. Parse/normalize the setting (compare host and port explicitly, and consider allowing subdomains) or validate its format when saved.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL is not a valid header value
findings.body: ALLOWALL is not a permitted X-Frame-Options value (the spec defines DENY, SAMEORIGIN, and ALLOW-FROM uri). Browsers currently ignore unrecognized values, which is why framing happens to work, but the behavior is undefined and stricter user agents or normalizing proxies may handle it differently. To allow cross-origin framing for this action, remove the X-Frame-Options header instead of setting an invalid value.

findings.title: Edits an already-deployed migration and adds force: true, which silently drops the table
findings.body: This changes 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb — a migration that has already run in deployed environments — to create_table :top_topics, force: true. force: true issues DROP TABLE IF EXISTS before creating, so anywhere the table exists while the migration is considered pending (db:schema:load followed by migrate, restored backups, staging/dev databases) the existing top_topics table is silently dropped and recreated. Where the migration already ran, the edit has no effect at all, making it misleading. Old migrations should not be edited; the new create_topic_embeds migration also does not need force: true.

findings.title: Blank embed_by_username silently no-ops, leaving an infinite reload/job loop
findings.body: When SiteSetting.embed_by_username is blank, fetch_http looks up User.where(username_lower: '') and returns without creating anything or logging why. The embed controller then keeps rendering loading.html.erb, which reloads the iframe every 30 seconds and enqueues a new RetrieveTopic job on every reload — forever, for every open browser tab on the embedding site. The controller or retriever should fail fast with a clear error (or gate the embed on embed_by_username being configured) instead of looping silently.
